This is performed by establishing virtual clusters on square grids and using the quality of intra- and inter-cluster communication to select the next hop to take, the simulation's outcome demonstrates that, while maintaining channel quality, the devised technique may advance the BS farther than the customary choices made by pertinent clustering route pick procedures. Additional simulation results demonstrate the improved energy economy, reduced latency, and dependability of the proposed method with randomly distributed barriers and nodes, The requirement for effective data transfer in remote sensor networks is currently being debated in the research sector. The result of the replication shows that, in comparison to the conventional options of significant grouping course pick activities, the developed plan may advance to the BS more quickly while maintaining channel quality. Additional recreation findings have shown the improved stability, reduced idle time, and increased energy efficiency of the given system randomly hubs and snagging dispersal.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security for IOMT Devices: Deep learning Techniques for Network Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: The increasing popularity of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, like wearable sensors, has greatly improved patient care by allowing continuous monitoring and real-time data transfer to the cloud. However, this progress also raises security concerns, as the data sent from these devices can be at risk of tampering or hacking during transmission. Keeping this sensitive medical data safe is crucial for patient safety. To address these issues, a fused CNN and LSTM are developed to check whether the data from wearable IoMT devices has been altered or attacked during transmission to the cloud. The CNN part of the model helps to pull out important features from the data, while the LSTM part looks for patterns to spot any signs of tampering. The model uses two convolutional layers each of which is followed by a MaxPooling layer. Our model, tested on a large dataset, achieved an accuracy of 97.06%, showing its ability to protect the integrity of transmitted medical data.

articleTitle: Analysis of using Zero Shot Open Vocabulary Detection Methods for Plastic Waste Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Pollution from plastic garbage has grown to be a major environmental issue, requiring the creation of effective techniques for identifying and categorizing it. Supervised machine learning is a proven technique for automatic waste detection and classification but requires heavy training. Unsupervised learning techniques such as transfer learning and few-shot learning (FSL) have greatly reduced the training time and the need for huge datasets. Vision Language Models (VLMs) with open vocabulary and zero-shot detection techniques have reduced the shortcomings of traditional models. This paper analyzes the scope of using zero-shot combined with open-vocabulary detection techniques such as YOLO World, Grounding DINO, ViLD, and OWL-ViT for plastic waste detection. Zero-shot open vocabulary models eliminate the need for training custom data for long hours, enabling models to classify new classes with only their semantic encoders and contrastive pre-training.

articleTitle: Data Clustering and Routing using Improved Water Wave Optimization in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are pivotal in various applications where data collection from distributed sensors is essential. However, optimizing data collection efficiency while preserving energy resources remains a challenge. A data clustering model proposed in this paper implements the concept of Water Wave Optimization (WWO) methodology. The purpose of using Water Wave Optimization in this paper is to improve the accuracy of data grouping. We have suggested a grouping model using WWO, the recommended method aims to improve the accuracy of data clustering. We have demonstrated the validity of the proposed idea through the Friedman test and statistical analysis. Experiments revealed that the suggested grouping model works, as evidenced by its higher accuracy rate. In the past decade, routing in Wireless Sensor Networks has emerged as the focus of most research. Implementing a routing model that can determine the most beneficial path depending on an assortment of performance parameters is an extensive task. Then it has been demonstrated that after being compared to the currently employed clustering approach, the accuracy and F-score rates of the proposed WWO techniques improved by an average of 4% and 7%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Dual-Layer Approach: Combining Lightweight and Dynamic RSA for Enhanced Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: An important aspect for both individuals and business data is security. Security has been studied extensively by many researchers. Security gaps or threats are ever increasing, and data protection is a primary issue. A lightweight hybrid cryptographic algorithm with two layers of encryption has been presented in this paper. A new effective, lightweight algorithm named ASCON-128 is used in the first layer, and a dynamic version of RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman) is used in the second layer. Asymmetric and symmetric cryptographic features have been combined by this approach. The proposed algorithm’s performance was evaluated using metrics such as execution time, throughput rate, delay, and latency. A higher level of security, a faster encryption execution times, reduced memory usages, and improved throughput were observed in the proposed algorithm when compared to widely used cryptographic systems. The resultsare shown by the experimental findings.

articleTitle: Leveraging Data Analytics to Enhance Athlete Performance in the UAE
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: This research paper aims to enhance cricket player performance through a comprehensive approach involving data-driven training and individualized injury prevention strategies. The primary objective is to optimize player performance by thoroughly assessing fitness levels, including strength, endurance, and flexibility. This enables the development of tailored training programs that address each player's specific needs, aiming to improve overall athletic performance. Additionally, this research focuses on identifying high-risk injury areas through advanced data analysis and tracking of injury history. By pinpointing these vulnerable regions, the study allows for targeted interventions and preventative measures designed to reduce injury risks and ensure consistent player availability. The effectiveness of customized injury prevention methods is compared to generic approaches, underscoring the advantages of personalized strategies. The study also contrasts traditional coaching methods with innovative data-driven strategies, highlighting how analytics can revolutionize both performance enhancement and injury prevention in cricket. Utilizing a mixed-methods research approach, this study analyzes data from 290 cricket players in the UAE, applying various statistical techniques, including descriptive statistics, regression analysis, correlation analysis, and significant T-tests, to validate the findings. This research not only provides valuable insights into the state of cricket in the UAE but also offers potential guidance for future studies and policy decisions related to sports performance and injury management. By integrating data-driven insights with personalized training and injury prevention, this project aims to make a significant contribution to the field of cricket, promoting advancements in player development and well-being.

articleTitle: Automated Leukaemia Cancer Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Leukaemia, a critical blood cancer, is marked by an excessive proliferation of immature white blood cells in the bone marrow, significantly impacting healthy cell function and presenting serious health risks. Early and accurate diagnosis of leukaemia remains a major challenge, with the disease categorized into acute and chronic forms, and acute lymphocytic leukaemia (ALL) accounting for around 25% of childhood cancer cases. This paper proposes a novel method for leukaemia detection using advanced deep learning techniques. We specifically use VGG19 and ResNet152, to analyze blood smear images and extract detailed features that enhance classification precision. Our approach is novel in integrating deep learning models with traditional machine learning classifiers, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, and AdaBoost. This hybrid method leverages the strengths of both deep learning for feature extraction and machine learning classifiers for enhanced classification, setting it apart from previous approaches that rely solely on deep learning models. The experimental results highlight the effectiveness of this deep learning-based approach in improving diagnostic accuracy and supporting effective clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Energy Data Transmission Using Intelligent-Based Techniques in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: The aim of the research is to use AI approaches to secure, energy and reliably transmit data on ad hoc networks. Ad hoc networks are becoming standard fare in contemporary communication infrastructures, wireless technology, and mobile devices. Protecting sensitive information during transmission is no simple task, especially in ad hoc networks due to their inherent instability and lack of central authority. The existing network can explain all the unknowns and complexity settings in Ad-HoC, conventional encryption techniques, and routing protocols. The proposed artificial intelligence-driven technique for ensuring safe and strong data transmission in various ad hoc network situations works by running comprehensive simulations and evaluations. For similarity metrics like packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay, and attack resilience, our findings show that the proposed framework outperforms conventional approaches an effectively without any delay and improve the speed of the data transmission.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of an Incremental Classifier using Clustered-C4.5 Algorithm for Processing Big Data Streams
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Currently, the inevitability of big data stream processing is increasingly becoming more critical and imperative due to the incremental nature of the heterogeneous and massive volume of data engendered by various sources. C4.5 is the most renowned algorithm to address the problem of data stream classification in online mode by constructing decision trees. But, the traditional C4.5 algorithm has a significant adverse impact on the speed of data stream processing in real-time scenarios. To handle this problem, we propose a new variant of the C4.5 classifier, named the Clustered-C4.5 (CC4.5) algorithm to classify data streams in online mode. This work integrates a Correlation-based Feature selection and Bat Optimization Technique (CFBOT) with the CC4.5 algorithm to improve the classification performance. The CFBOT is employed to measure the dependencies among selected features and to determine the ideal subset for training and testing tasks. Meanwhile, CC4.5 organizes the data into smaller clusters instead of building a single decision tree. The integration of the CC4.5 algorithm and CFBOT helps the system classify imbalanced and multi-class datasets effectively. The performance of the proposed classifier is cautiously studied on the real-world dataset (i.e., UCI-heart disease dataset) by relating its enactment with many state-of-the-art approaches regarding classification accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and intersection over-union (IoU). Additionally, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test is employed to assess whether our classification technique offers a statistically significant improvement over other classifier methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed classifier outperforms other approaches with superior accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUC, and IoU of 93.6%, 96.2%, 79.3%, 92.3%, and 90.3%, correspondingly. Accordingly, we can conclude that CC4.5 is the better data stream classification model related to classification approaches recently reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for resource allocation in Cloud: Review and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is robust to trend changes in dynamic cloud environments. The combination of Deep Neural Networks for learning the Q values in Reinforcement Learning with regular updates to the trained model shows promising results in reducing makespan and energy consumption. Vanilla DRL and various schemes that address shortcomings in the basic DRL are analyzed for the scheduling of tasks in cloud. The design parameters of the neural network and reinforcement learning are compared to present configurations that work well for a particular cloud environment. The advantages and shortcomings of the approaches are highlighted and scrutinized compared to several baseline algorithms. The OpenAI Gym package is discussed to give novice researchers insight into how to start work on DRLs. The prospects of applying DRL in cloud scheduling are put forth for researchers to construct efficient learning networks for efficient task scheduling.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Wireless Power Transmission for Enhanced Mobile Charging Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing & Industry 6.0 (C2I6)
abstract: Wireless power transmission (WPT) is an emerging technology that enables the transfer of electrical energy from a power source to a device without the need for physical connectors. This project focuses on the design and implementation of a WPT system tailored for mobile phone charging. The system operates on the principle of electromagnetic induction, where energy is transmitted through an oscillating magnetic field generated by a transmitter coil and captured by a receiver coil. The transmitter side begins with a DC power supply that is converted into AC by a transmitter circuit. This AC current generates an oscillating magnetic field via the transmitter coil, which serves as the medium for energy transmission. On the receiver side, the receiver coil captures this magnetic field, inducing an AC current, which is then rectified back into DC by the receiver circuit. This DC power is then used to charge a mobile phone. This wireless charging system offers several advantages, including the elimination of physical connectors, reducing wear and tear on devices, and enhancing user convenience. The project not only demonstrates the basic principles of WPT but also explores its practical application in everyday life, paving the way for future advancements in wireless charging technologies.
